prerequisite: Run extract_measured_sections first to see the calibration state and crest elevations, then set strip_threshold_elev / bottom_elev from that
fixture_requirements: The same survey drawing as extract_measured_sections (same layer and title conventions)
At least one section whose crest is above strip_threshold_elev (produces a strip segment)
At least one section whose ground width exceeds +/- excavation_half_width (triggers the slope branch)
At least one section that failed calibration (verifies the skipped branch)
assertions: In-memory change only: results must be kept with an explicit save_dwg
sections_processed + sections_skipped == number of sections matching line_filter
sections that failed calibration all count toward sections_skipped, have skipped=true with a report in per_section, get a warning entry, and nothing is drawn for them
strip lines go on strip_line_layer, cut lines on excavation_line_layer, hatches on hatch_layer, labels on annotation_layer, centrelines on centerline_layer; all five layers are created automatically
the offset part of a strip line = that ground segment shifted down by strip_thickness (verify per point: elevation difference == strip_thickness)
strip intervals = maximal intervals where ground elevation > strip_threshold_elev; intervals narrower than 0.01 are discarded
with strip_threshold_elev above the crest, strip_lines == 0 and that section's strip_intervals is an empty array
with strip_thickness = 0 the strip line coincides with the ground line and the area is 0 (the edge value must not throw)
cut lines are limited to +/- excavation_half_width; an end within the limit lands directly at (interval end, bottom_elev)
an end beyond the limit slopes at 1:slope_ratio_m up to the stripped surface; the third element of per_section excavation_intervals marks 'left slope' / 'right slope'
when a slope does not daylight, warnings contain 'left slope not daylighted' or 'right slope not daylighted' and that end degenerates to the last surface point (not silent)
cut intervals are taken where the stripped surface is above bottom_elev, not the original ground (strip first, then cut; the order cannot be reversed)
with bottom_elev above the crest the section has no cut interval and counts toward sections_zero_excavation
bottom_elev_by_section matches the full title first, then the survey line name, and only then falls back to the global bottom_elev
a non-numeric value in bottom_elev_by_section throws and names the key
with draw_hatch=false hatches == 0 but the design lines are still drawn
a hatch failure does not abort the batch: that section has one hatch fewer and its design lines remain (catch branch in DikeHatch)
with draw_labels=false labels == 0
with text_style empty, texts use the drawing's current default style (db.Textstyle) and are not forced
with text_style naming an existing style, the drawn texts' TextStyleId points to it
with text_style naming a missing style, throw and suggest changing the parameter or running normalize_textstyles first (no silent fallback to the default)
rerun with clear_existing=true deletes only Polyline/Hatch/DBText on the five target layers; other layers and other object types are untouched
Idempotent: two runs with the same parameters give the same strip_lines / excavation_lines / hatches / labels and nothing stacks
rerun with clear_existing=false stacks (used to confirm the clearing switch really works)
strip_thickness < 0 throws
slope_ratio_m <= 0 throws
excavation_half_width <= 0 throws
hatch_scale <= 0 throws
text_height <= 0 throws
no ground line on ground_layer throws and names ground_layer
line_filter matching nothing throws and reports the total section count
the drawn lines can be edited by hand: downstream compute_embankment_demolition reads the lines in the drawing, not this node's in-memory result
